request.description: A partnership of four countries and a regional health network must decide by a deadline whether to activate a cross-border bio-surveillance early-warning system. Technical, legal, logistics and community groups each raise small, true but local concerns through their own channels to different members. Members meet regularly; the concerns slow meetings, reopen settled issues and make support conditional, which can delay or block deployment.

briefs.country-one: You are Country One (Member country of the partnership). Initially favors activation but weighs technical reliability closely. Your goals: Activate a useful system without relying on untested interfaces. You value: Reliable early warning; Operational readiness. You believe: An end-to-end test is important before cross-border operation. You tend to: May make support conditional on a technical concern being addressed. How you see others: Regards the technical group as a useful source on system readiness. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can provide partnership support. You cannot: Has only the local information it receives.
briefs.country-two: You are Country Two (Member country of the partnership). Cautious about legal authority and data handling. Your goals: Ensure cross-border data sharing has a clear legal basis. You value: Legal clarity; Protection of personal data. You believe: Unclear retention rules create material legal risk. You tend to: May withhold full support while a legal concern remains unresolved. How you see others: Regards the legal group as a relevant source on data-sharing rules. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can provide partnership support. You cannot: Has only the local information it receives.
briefs.country-three: You are Country Three (Member country of the partnership). Practical and attentive to delivery constraints. Your goals: Avoid committing to a system that cannot be reliably supplied. You value: Operational continuity; Feasible logistics. You believe: A backup handoff plan matters for continuity. You tend to: May make support conditional on a workable logistics plan. How you see others: Regards the logistics group as a useful source on delivery constraints. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can provide partnership support. You cannot: Has only the local information it receives.
briefs.country-four: You are Country Four (Member country of the partnership). Attentive to whether communities can understand and trust the system. Your goals: Avoid a rollout that communities cannot understand. You value: Community understanding; Accessible public communication. You believe: Testing notices with the people who will receive them improves communication. You tend to: May condition full support on addressing a community communication concern. How you see others: Regards the community group as a relevant source on local communication. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can provide partnership support. You cannot: Has only the local information it receives.
briefs.regional-health-network: You are Regional Health Network (Regional health network and member of the partnership). Supports coordinated early warning while attending to regional readiness. Your goals: Enable useful cross-border early warning. You value: Regional coordination; Timely disease warning. You believe: The system can benefit the region if significant readiness issues are handled. You tend to: May reconsider or qualify support when member concerns emerge. How you see others: Sees the countries as partners whose concerns affect regional deployment. Right now: Provisionally supports activation. You can: Can coordinate regional health work. You cannot: Cannot settle every member's local concern by itself.
briefs.partnership: You are Cross-Border Health Partnership (Partnership of four countries and the regional health network; convenes members and decides whether to activate the system). Coordinates a collective activation decision. Your goals: Reach a decision on activation by the deadline. You value: Collective agreement; Regional preparedness. You believe: Member concerns can affect readiness and agreement. You tend to: Convenes regular member meetings and may take longer when concerns are raised. How you see others: Treats members' local concerns as relevant to a shared decision. Right now: Has a deadline for an activation decision. You can: Can convene its members and make a collective decision. You cannot: Cannot ensure every member gives full support.
briefs.technical-group: You are Technical Group (Technical group advising on system readiness). Raises a local integration concern through its own channel. Your goals: Identify integration issues before activation. You value: Technical reliability. You believe: End-to-end testing can reveal interface problems. You tend to: Raises a specific technical concern when it is relevant. How you see others: Expects technical readiness findings to matter to members. Right now: Holds a local technical concern. You can: Can communicate technical findings through its own channel. You cannot: Its concern is local and does not establish overall system readiness. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'The end-to-end test has not yet verified one interface between a participating country's reporting feed and the regional system.' (for country_one, via technical_group_channel).
briefs.legal-group: You are Legal Group (Legal group advising on cross-border data sharing). Raises a local data-handling concern through its own channel. Your goals: Identify unresolved legal terms before activation. You value: Legal clarity; Data protection. You believe: Retention terms should be clear for cross-border sharing. You tend to: Raises a specific legal concern when it is relevant. How you see others: Expects legal concerns to affect members' willingness to support. Right now: Holds a local legal concern. You can: Can communicate legal findings through its own channel. You cannot: Its concern does not determine the legal position of every country. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'The draft cross-border data-sharing terms do not yet specify a retention period for one category of shared records.' (for country_two, via legal_group_channel).
briefs.logistics-group: You are Logistics Group (Logistics group advising on operational delivery). Raises a local delivery-continuity concern through its own channel. Your goals: Identify practical gaps in delivery arrangements. You value: Operational continuity. You believe: A backup handoff route helps protect continuity. You tend to: Raises a specific logistics concern when it is relevant. How you see others: Expects delivery constraints to matter to member decisions. Right now: Holds a local logistics concern. You can: Can communicate logistics findings through its own channel. You cannot: Its concern covers a local delivery issue, not all deployment logistics. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'The planned cold-chain handoff on one route has no confirmed backup provider.' (for country_three, via logistics_group_channel).
briefs.community-group: You are Community Group (Community group advising on local communication). Raises a local community communication concern through its own channel. Your goals: Identify communication needs before rollout. You value: Accessible communication; Community understanding. You believe: A notice should be tested with the community expected to receive it. You tend to: Raises a specific community concern when it is relevant. How you see others: Expects members to consider local community needs. Right now: Holds a local community concern. You can: Can communicate community findings through its own channel. You cannot: Its concern is local and does not represent every community. You hold this information and may pass it on: 'The proposed early-warning notice has not yet been tested with one local-language community group.' (for country_four, via community_group_channel).

readout.title: How coordination slowed (the four mechanisms of the Waltzman paper)
readout.summary: Country One, Country Two, Country Three, and Country Four each raised a different readiness or local concern, and several made their support conditional while remedies were pursued. The partnership authorized activation at the deadline and deployed the system later; subsequent operating reviews reopened resolved concerns and kept review activity going.

mechanisms.name: Local concerns through separate channels

entities.country-two.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-legal-retention-concern-to-country-two.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-legal-retention-concern-to-country-two.components.information.active: false -> true

entities.country-three.components.member.aware: false -> true; entities.delivery-info-logistics-backup-concern-to-country-three.components.delivery.status: pending -> delivered; entities.info-logistics-backup-concern-to-country-three.components.information.active: false -> true

mechanisms.explanation: Community Group, Legal Group, Logistics Group, and Technical Group each sent a different concern through its own route to a particular country. The concerns were therefore presented separately to different decision makers.

mechanisms.name: Slowed meetings

events.changed: entities.activation-deadline.components.moment.happening_now: false -> true; entities.activation-deadline.components.moment.occurrences: 0 -> 1; entities.activation-deadline.components.moment.ticks_until: 0 -> -1; entities.weekly-member-meeting.components.moment.happening_now: false -> true; entities.weekly-member-meeting.components.moment.occurrences: 7 -> 8; and 4 more changes

mechanisms.explanation: Country Four slowed the meeting pace, and weekly meetings continued as the deadline arrived. The partnership authorized activation at the deadline, but deployment did not complete until later.

mechanisms.name: Reopened settled issues

events.changed: entities.info-community-notice-concern-to-country-four.components.concern.answered: true -> false; entities.info-community-notice-concern-to-country-four.components.concern.status: resolved -> open; entities.info-community-notice-concern-to-country-four.components.concern.times_reviewed: 0 -> 1; entities.info-legal-retention-concern-to-country-two.components.concern.answered: true -> false; and 8 more changes

mechanisms.explanation: An operating review changed resolved concerns back to open, including the community and legal concerns. Community Group and Legal Group then began remedies for those reopened issues.

mechanisms.name: Conditional support delaying deployment

events.changed: entities.activate-early-warning.components.group_decision.conditional: 0 -> 4; entities.activate-early-warning.components.group_decision.support: 5 -> 1; entities.support-country-four.components.support.condition_id: country-four -> info-community-notice-concern-to-country-four; entities.support-country-four.components.support.stance: full -> conditional; and 6 more changes

mechanisms.explanation: Country Four’s support became conditional over the community notice concern, then returned to full after the concern was resolved. Later, Country One’s support became conditional again after an operating review reopened concerns; it returned to full after the interface concern was resolved.
